tasks.short: Teach and monitor safe equipment use

steps.what: Instruct and monitor students using equipment and materials, correcting unsafe handling immediately

tasks.design: Keep equipment instruction and live supervision with the teacher. Digital materials do not replace observing students or intervening during practical work.
tasks.previous_blocker: The teacher must see what students actually do around equipment.
tasks.enabler_now: No supplied evidence establishes replacement of this direct supervision.
tasks.still_hard: Recognise a misunderstanding before it causes injury or damage.
tasks.human_edge: Intervene promptly and adapt the demonstration to the learner.
tasks.altitude: Improve practical instruction and intervention quality.

reach.learn: Recognise when to stop work and call the teacher

evidence.claim: Practical equipment instruction and monitoring remain direct teaching work; no task labour saving is established.

assumptions: The teacher observes student actions and assesses safe practice within s1; no structured competence or safety flag is assumed.
Preparing teaching materials is a separate task and receives no savings here.
No added deployment or operating process means upkeep is zero.
research_questions: Which handling errors require repeated demonstration?

incremental.description: No additional system or operating work

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100: all direct equipment instruction and supervision remains; zero gross and net savings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Select curriculum aims and establish practical constraints for lessons, units and projects
Draft objectives with observable outcomes and explicit links to selected curriculum aims

loop.purpose: Propose clear wording for teacher selected learning objectives
loop.input: Teacher selected aims, class context and practical constraints
loop.output: Candidate objectives with aim references and observable outcomes
loop.check: Teacher verifies aim coverage, practical feasibility, clarity and suitability for this class
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; unsupported or unsuitable objectives are written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Reuse curriculum wording and native templates first; only contextual wording needs drafting

steps.what: Establish final objectives and communicate them to students with examples and clarification

tasks.design: Use {DOCS} templates and a bounded drafting step to propose wording for teacher selected aims. The teacher checks suitability, establishes the final objectives and explains them to students.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clear objective wording must connect broad aims to a particular practical lesson.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting tools can suggest contextual wording while leaving selection and teaching judgement with the teacher.
tasks.still_hard: Choose goals that are achievable and useful for these learners.
tasks.human_edge: Know what students need to understand before beginning practical work.
tasks.altitude: Own the connection between curriculum aims and observable learning.

reach.learn: Check alignment without prescribing the same lesson for every class

evidence.claim: Snappet's Copilot suggests arithmetic lessons that teachers accept or change; this does not establish vocational objective drafting savings.
Contextual objective wording and the proposed labour scenario are E1 model knowledge.

assumptions: In s1 the teacher supplies aim codes and text, lesson scope, time, equipment limits and relevant class context. Selection, capture and clarification are counted in 35 hours.
No pupil level or competence classification is inferred. Use class context without unnecessary pupil identifiers.
s2 retains 21 hours for wording review and correction; s3 separately retains the decision and student explanation.
Native templates and existing objectives are reused before model drafting. Missing aims or unsuitable suggestions return to manual writing.
unknowns: Amount of new objective wording versus reuse
research_questions: Does checked drafting save time while keeping objectives feasible and understandable?

already_counted.description: Aim selection, brief capture, wording checks and student explanation

incremental.description: Prompt and aim list upkeep plus sampled objective review

approvals.approved_version: Exact objectives, aim references and class lesson context; edits invalidate approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 task scenarios: B=100, R=91 yields 9 gross and 3 net after 6 focal upkeep hours. Range 0-2 reflects substantial selection and communication work and reusable existing objectives.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Observe and evaluate students' performance, behavior, social development and physical health in context

tasks.design: Keep contextual observation and evaluation with the teacher. A pupil record system can store observations but does not produce them.
tasks.previous_blocker: Understanding a pupil requires direct observation and professional context.
tasks.enabler_now: No supplied evidence establishes replacement of that judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Avoid drawing broad conclusions from isolated behavior.
tasks.human_edge: Notice changes and consider explanations before deciding on follow up.
tasks.altitude: Improve the quality and limits of observations.

evidence.claim: ParnasSys provides pupil records and learning goal tracking; storage does not establish automated developmental judgement.
Retaining observation and evaluation establishes no labour saving in this task.

assumptions: The teacher produces observations and evaluation during s1; no structured behavior, health or emotional state flag is assumed.
Record maintenance and separate class work grading own their respective baselines; this task adds no clerical saving.
No deployment means no additional upkeep.
research_questions: How are observations checked before consequential conclusions are drawn?

incremental.description: No added system or monitoring work

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100: contextual observation and evaluation remain fully human; zero gross and net savings.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Assign and grade class work and homework

steps.what: Assign class work and homework and verify closed item keys and marking rules
outputs: checked closed item key and roster mapping

steps.what: Calculate provisional closed item marks from submitted answers and the checked key
inputs: checked closed item key and roster mapping

steps.what: Grade open work, check provisional marks and approve feedback before releasing grades

tasks.design: Configure exact closed item marking in {LMS}; assignment and answer context remain available in {DOCS}. The teacher retains open and practical work grading and approves all released grades and feedback.
tasks.previous_blocker: Simple answer comparisons may be repeated manually alongside substantive grading.
tasks.enabler_now: Native closed item scoring can apply a teacher verified key without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Assess practical understanding and provide useful feedback.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise reasoning that an exact answer key cannot capture.
tasks.altitude: Focus grading effort on evidence of understanding and exceptions.

evidence.claim: Closed item scoring can follow an explicit key while open and practical work remain teacher judgement; this task's savings are E1 model knowledge.

assumptions: In s1 the teacher produces item identifiers, correct answers, point weights, assignment identifier and roster mapping. Key creation, capture, checking and missing identity resolution are included in 30 hours.

After assignment, students produce submitted answers through their unchanged learning activity. The platform records answer, pupil and assignment identifiers; answers are not assumed available before s1.
Paper or unmatched responses go to manual grading in s3, which includes necessary transcription. No automated competence judgement or open answer scoring is proposed.
Native platform marking is used first. Sites already using it have zero incremental saving.
General developmental observation belongs only to task 6619; this task owns marking submitted work.
unknowns: Share of work suitable for exact keys
research_questions: Does exact scoring save time after key preparation, identity checks and grade approval?

already_counted.description: Assignment, key capture, open grading and final grade checks

incremental.description: Key upkeep and sampled scoring reconciliation

approvals.approved_version: Exact pupil, assignment, grades and feedback; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 task scenarios: B=100, R=75 yields 25 gross and 17 net after 8 focal upkeep hours. Range 0-4 allows practical and open work to dominate and closed scoring to exist already.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Use checked drafting and exact scoring for small repeatable components while protecting supervision and professional observation.
reach: Help assistants preserve work identity and distinguish observation from interpretation
role.ambitious_version: A teacher with less repeat wording and answer comparison and preserved time for students' practical learning.
